description: How every vdocs search front door (the MCP search tool and `vdocs ask`, vdocs-web, vdocs-cli) turns typed keywords into an SQLite FTS5 MATCH expression. Each case gives the query and the two expressions every reader must produce exactly: `all` (searched first) and `any` (the fallback, searched only when `all` matches nothing; empty when there is no fallback). vdocs runs every case in tests/unit/server/test_query_reader.py; consumers copy this file by hand, as they copy contracts/read/v1.json, and run every case in their own tests, including the `synonyms` cases. Keyword-search proposal, fix 2 (docs/proposals/keyword-search-five-fixes.md).
rules: Split the query at every double quote. Pieces at odd positions are quoted; a quote left open runs to the end of the query.
A quoted piece is one exact phrase. Outside quotes, words are separated by whitespace.
A word that is exactly AND, OR or NOT, in capitals, is an operator. In lower case it is an ordinary word. Inside quotes it is part of the phrase.
Every other word, and every quoted piece, becomes one phrase of its letter-and-digit runs joined by single spaces, keeping the case typed: DG*5.3*1029 becomes "DG 5 3 1029", x-ray becomes "x ray".
A piece with no letters or digits is skipped.
A word outside quotes whose only run is a single character is skipped, unless the word contains one of * ^ # . $ % / (so #5 is kept and I is skipped).

Terms are joined by the operator typed between them, or by AND when none was typed. When several operators are typed in a row, the last one counts. An operator before the first term or after the last is dropped.
The output is each term as a double-quoted phrase, joined by ' AND ', ' OR ' or ' NOT '. FTS5 binds NOT tightest, then AND, then OR.
`any` is the same terms joined by ' OR ' when no operator was typed and there are at least two terms; otherwise it is empty.
Synonyms (fix 3) apply only with a synonym table; the `cases` use none, and the `synonyms` section below gives its rules, a fixed table and its own cases.

rules: A synonym table is rows of (term, alternative, match_case), in order. A term is a phrase of letter-and-digit runs joined by single spaces, of at least two characters. match_case 0: the term matches typed words in any case. match_case 1: only as written (application codes, namespaces, product abbreviations).

Outside quotes, at each word that is not an operator, take the longest run of consecutive non-operator words whose letter-and-digit runs, joined by single spaces, equal a term (exactly for match_case 1, ignoring case for 0). The run becomes one term. When no run matches, the word follows the rules above.

The term's alternatives are its rows' alternatives in table order (match_case 1 rows first, then match_case 0), each written as a phrase of its letter-and-digit runs. Drop an alternative that equals the typed run ignoring case, one that is AND, OR or NOT in any case, and a repeat ignoring case.

With alternatives left, the term is the typed run's phrase and the alternatives' phrases joined by ' OR ' in parentheses: ("blood bank" OR "VBECS"). With none left, it is the typed run's phrase alone.
Text in double quotes is never expanded. The term counts as one term for the joins and for `any`.

cases.all: ("blood bank" OR "VistA Blood Establishment Computer Software" OR "VBECS") AND "ISBT"
cases.any: ("blood bank" OR "VistA Blood Establishment Computer Software" OR "VBECS") OR "ISBT"
